spec_notes: docs/shiploop/spec.md is short (R-1..R-3) and does not contradict the request. It decides without marking them as choices: trimming of names, 409 for resolved/closed, that "all supported filters intersect" (which changes the 1.4.0 status+priority answer from union to intersection), the CLI placeholder and a blank fifth raw field. It is silent on keeping the assignee through the lifecycle, on show, on POST/PATCH refusing assignee, and on the later rules recorded only in docs/shiploop/fix.md (em dash refusal, Unicode line breaks, surrogates, repeated filters matching every value). Pins a choice a correct product need not share: docs/shiploop/architecture.md AD-1 puts the audit sequence in the notification key; spec R-1 says unassigning is audited but does not say whether it notifies.
tests_notes: TC-1, TC-2, TC-3 and TC-5 each cover many behaviours (TC-5 spans persistence, legacy files, HTTP, both CLI forms and the weekly report). TC-6 is tied to internals: it builds TicketStore with a fake persistence and asserts outbox event id 2; the assignee.test.js tests compare store.snapshot(). Tests that would fail on another correct build: the em dash refusal test, the repeated-filter test (a build using the first value fails it), the Unicode line break and surrogate refusals, TC-2's 64 x U+10400 accepted (a build counting UTF-16 units refuses it), TC-1's trimmed "  Dana Lee  " stored as "Dana Lee", TC-4's three distinct notifications (a build keyed by agent may send fewer, which the inventory accepts), TC-5's em dash and empty fifth raw field.
maintainer: store.apply() now replaces the ticket object and, on a failed save, rebuilds the AuditLog and Outbox from JSON copies; every mutation goes through it, so a change there affects create, update, transition and assign alike. The em dash marker couples API validation (src/tickets/validate.js requires src/format.js) to CLI display, and the same validator runs at start on stored data, so changing the marker or the name rules can stop existing data files from loading. The all-values rule for repeated filters lives in one generic reader shared by status, priority and assignee.
